Q908: Port city on the Don River in southern Russia, near the Sea of Azov.
Founded in 1749 as a customs post; grew as a grain-trading centre.
Hosted 2018 World Cup matches; headquarters of Russia's Southern Military District.
Q6905368: The municipality of Monterrey, capital of Nuevo León in northern Mexico.
Founded in 1596; the saddle-shaped Cerro de la Silla mountain is its symbol.
Mexico's main industrial city, home of Cemex and FEMSA (Coca-Cola bottler).
Q855997: City in central Punjab, Pakistan; one of the country's planned cities.
Called the 'City of Eagles' for its large Pakistan Air Force base.
A big citrus-growing area famous for kinnow mandarins.
Q43668: The largest city in Kentucky, on the Ohio River.
Hosts the Kentucky Derby, America's most famous horse race, at Churchill Downs.
Home of the Louisville Slugger baseball bat and much of the bourbon industry.
Birthplace of boxer Muhammad Ali; the airport is named after him.
Q162880: City in northwestern Shandong on the Grand Canal.
Called 'China's Solar Valley' for its solar water heater industry.
The tomb of a 15th-century king of Sulu (Philippines), who died while visiting China, is here.
Q83061: City in eastern Turkey on the shore of Lake Van, Turkey's largest lake.
As Tushpa it was the capital of the Urartu kingdom (9th–6th centuries BC); the Van Fortress survives.
Famous for the Van cat with odd-coloured eyes, and for its breakfasts.
Akdamar Island in the lake has a 10th-century Armenian church.
Q71247: City in southern Hubei on the Yangtze.
Its ancient name Jiangling was the capital of the Chu state; it has one of China's best-preserved city walls.
A key city in the Three Kingdoms story ('Guan Yu loses Jingzhou').
The Jingzhou Museum holds a 2,000-year-old preserved Han-dynasty body.
Q1015805: County-level city in Jiangsu under Suzhou; the name means 'always ripe' (good harvests).
A centre of clothing manufacturing with a huge garment market.
Home of Yushan hill and the Song-dynasty Fangta pagoda.
Q388108: City on the Nile in Upper Egypt, capital of Sohag Governorate.
Near the White and Red Monasteries, some of Egypt's oldest Coptic monasteries.
Abydos, with the Temple of Seti I, is in the governorate.
Q42061: Satellite city northwest of Seoul in Gyeonggi Province.
Includes Ilsan, a planned new town, and the KINTEX exhibition centre.
Hosts the Goyang International Flower Festival at Ilsan Lake Park.
Q1741227: Includes the Kilamba new city, a huge housing project built by Chinese companies around 2011.
The name means 'land of Kilamba' in Kimbundu.
Q180078: City in western Iran, a centre of Kurdish culture.
The Behistun inscription of Darius I, key to deciphering cuneiform, is nearby (World Heritage Site).
Taq-e Bostan has Sasanian rock reliefs.
Q51698: City in the Rio Grande Valley of Texas, opposite Reynosa, Mexico.
A cross-border trade and shopping hub.
Called the 'City of Palms'; the area grows citrus fruit.
Q585: Capital of Norway, at the head of the Oslofjord.
Founded around 1040; rebuilt after a fire in 1624 and called Christiania until 1925.
The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded here; the Viking Ship Museum and Munch's 'The Scream' are here.
Hosted the 1952 Winter Olympics; famous for the Holmenkollen ski jump.
Q465022: Capital of Enugu State in southeastern Nigeria; called the 'Coal City'.
Founded in 1909 after coal was discovered; the 1949 Iva Valley shooting of coal miners fuelled nationalism.
Was the capital of Biafra at the start of the Nigerian Civil War (1967).
Its name means 'top of the hill' in Igbo.
Q188693: Malawi's commercial capital and second city.
Founded in 1876 by Scottish missionaries; named after Blantyre in Scotland, birthplace of David Livingstone.
Its St Michael and All Angels Church was built by missionaries without architects (1891).
Q210307: City in the State of Mexico, on the eastern edge of Mexico City.
Built on the dried bed of Lake Texcoco; grew from informal settlements since the 1950s.
Named after Nezahualcóyotl, the 15th-century poet-king of Texcoco.
One of the most densely populated areas in Mexico.
Q633530: City in West Bengal, headquarters of Murshidabad district.
Murshidabad, the last capital of independent Bengal's Nawabs, is nearby.
Was an early British East India Company cantonment; the 1857 rebellion's first stirrings were here.
Famous for silk and sweets like chhanabora.
Q237847: City in southern Maharashtra near Karnataka.
Famous for Solapuri chaddars (cotton bedsheets) and towels.
Was briefly self-governing during the 1930 Civil Disobedience movement ('Solapur Martial Law').
A big centre of hand-rolled bidi making.
Q1953: Capital of Armenia, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
Founded as the fortress Erebuni in 782 BC — older than Rome.
Called the 'Pink City' for its pink tuff stone buildings; Mount Ararat is visible across the Turkish border.
The Matenadaran holds one of the largest collections of ancient manuscripts.
Q212938: The part of Jerusalem east of the 1949 armistice line, including the walled Old City.
Holds the Temple Mount / al-Haram al-Sharif with the Dome of the Rock and Al-Aqsa Mosque, the Western Wall and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.
Taken by Israel in 1967 and later annexed; most countries consider it occupied territory.
Claimed by Palestinians as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Q657461: Port city on Colombia's Caribbean coast.
Founded in 1533; a key Spanish port for shipping silver to Spain and a major slave-trade port.
Its walled old city and fortresses (Castillo San Felipe) are a World Heritage Site.
Setting of many works by Gabriel García Márquez, who lived there.
Q266014: City in southern Hunan where the Xiao and Xiang rivers meet.
The Tang writer Liu Zongyuan was exiled here and wrote the famous 'Eight Records of Yongzhou'.
The Nüshu script, a writing system used only by women, comes from Jiangyong county here.
Q134291: Port city on Turkey's Mediterranean coast; its port is one of the largest in Turkey.
Tarsus, birthplace of the Apostle Paul, is part of the metro area.
Known for tantuni street food and the coastal ruins of Soli.
Q648: City in French Flanders near the Belgian border, capital of the Hauts-de-France region.
Was Flemish (Rijsel) until Louis XIV captured it in 1667; its Vauban citadel survives.
Hosts the Braderie, Europe's largest flea market, every September; connected to London and Brussels by Eurostar.
Q426756: City in Sichuan between Chengdu and Chongqing.
Called the 'Sweet City' for its sugar cane production.
Hometown of the painter Zhang Daqian.
Q963782: County-level city in Guangxi under Guigang.
Jintian village here is where Hong Xiuquan launched the Taiping Rebellion in 1851.
Known for Xishan tea and the Xishan scenic mountain.
Q416669: City in Hunan on the Zi River near Dongting Lake.
Famous for Anhua dark tea, a fermented tea.
Q3426: City in southwestern Russia on the Voronezh River near the Don.
Peter the Great built Russia's first navy fleet here in 1696 for the Azov campaigns.
Heavily destroyed in WWII; a front line in 1942–43.
Known for its fertile black soil (chernozem) region.
Q915: City on the Kama River near the Ural Mountains.
Near the Perm-36 Gulag camp museum and the Kungur Ice Cave.
A centre of oil, chemicals and aircraft engines; associated with the setting of Pasternak's 'Doctor Zhivago'.
Q101625: City at the foot of the Atlas Mountains; one of Morocco's four imperial cities.
Founded around 1070 by the Almoravids; called the 'Red City' for its red walls.
Jemaa el-Fnaa square, with storytellers and food stalls, is UNESCO intangible heritage.
The Koutoubia Mosque and the Majorelle Garden are landmarks; gave its name to Morocco ('Marrakesh').
Q515573: City in southwestern Shaanxi on the Han River, between the Qinling and Daba mountains.
Liu Bang was King of Han here before founding the Han dynasty, which gave the Han Chinese their name.
Burial place of Zhuge Liang at Mount Dingjun.
Famous for crested ibis conservation and rapeseed flower fields.
Q170578: Capital of Sergipe, Brazil's smallest state.
Founded in 1855 as a planned capital with a grid of streets.
Known for its long Atalaia beach and crab dishes.
Q25563103: Capital of the Kakatiya dynasty (12th–14th centuries); its Kakatiya Arch is on Telangana's emblem.
Nearby Ramappa Temple is a World Heritage Site; the Thousand Pillar Temple is in the city.
Home of an NIT engineering institute.
Q7880: France's fourth city, on the Garonne in the southwest.
Called the 'Pink City' for its brick buildings; the Basilica of Saint-Sernin is a World Heritage Site.
Europe's aerospace capital: headquarters of Airbus and a big space centre.
Capital of the Visigothic Kingdom in the 5th century; known for rugby and cassoulet.
Q71305: City in eastern Hubei on the Yangtze, next to Wuhan.
Was briefly the capital of the Wu state in the Three Kingdoms (as Wuchang).
Home of Ezhou Huahu Airport, Asia's first dedicated cargo hub airport (opened 2022).
Q173545: City on the Orontes River in west-central Syria.
Famous for its giant wooden water wheels (norias), some over 20 m high.
Site of the 1982 Hama massacre, when the government crushed an uprising.
Known for halawet el jibn, a cheese-based sweet.
Q273014: Port city in Tamaulipas on the Pánuco River near the Gulf of Mexico.
During Mexico's first oil boom (around 1920) it was one of the busiest oil-export ports in the world.
Its centre has French-style balconied buildings; known for 'tortas de la barda'.
Q243325: Third-largest metro area of Bangladesh, on the Rupsha River.
Gateway to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest and home of the Bengal tiger.
Near the Port of Mongla and the Sixty Dome Mosque in Bagerhat (World Heritage Site).
Centre of shrimp farming and jute processing.
Q1344683: County-level city in Shandong under Tai'an.
Where the 'Xintai Man' fossils (about 50,000 years old) were found.
Q165341: Capital of Piauí, the only northeastern Brazilian state capital not on the coast.
Founded in 1852 as one of Brazil's first planned cities; named after Empress Teresa Cristina.
Called the 'Green City' for its trees; one of the hottest cities in Brazil.
Lies between the Parnaíba and Poti rivers.
Q197377: County-level city and Yangtze port under Suzhou.
One of China's richest county-level cities; home of Shagang, one of the biggest private steel companies.
Known as a model 'civilised city' in China.
Q53077: Capital of Coahuila in northern Mexico.
Called the 'Detroit of Mexico' for its car and truck factories (GM, Stellantis, Daimler).
Famous for colourful sarape blankets and the Museo del Desierto with dinosaur fossils.
Founded in 1577, one of the oldest cities in northern Mexico.
Q39121: The largest city in Yorkshire, on the River Aire.
Grew with wool and flax mills in the Industrial Revolution.
Marks & Spencer started as a market stall in Leeds Kirkgate Market in 1884.
A big financial and university city; the world's oldest surviving film was shot here in 1888.
Q8969: The largest city of Quintana Roo, on the Caribbean coast of the Yucatán Peninsula.
Built from scratch as a planned tourist resort since 1970.
Its Hotel Zone lies on a narrow strip of sand between the sea and a lagoon.
Gateway to the Riviera Maya, Tulum and Chichén Itzá.
Q12892: Belgium's largest municipality and second city, on the Scheldt.
Its port is the second-largest in Europe.
The world's diamond capital: most of the world's rough diamonds are traded here.
Home of the painter Rubens; the Cathedral of Our Lady is the tallest church in the Low Countries.
Q572014: City in northeastern Guangxi bordering Hunan and Guangdong.
Huangyao ancient town is a well-preserved Ming–Qing village.
Known for marble and granite processing.
Q181966: Capital of Okinawa Prefecture, on Okinawa Island.
The main trading port of the Ryukyu Kingdom; Shuri Castle was its royal palace (burned in 2019, being rebuilt).
Heavily damaged in the 1945 Battle of Okinawa; under US administration until 1972.
Kokusai-dori is its main shopping street.
Q323801: Mozambique's third city and the main centre of the north.
Linked by road and railway to the port of Nacala and to Malawi.
Home to the Makua people; its cathedral is one of the largest in Mozambique.
Q243327: Capital of South Gyeongsang Province, on Masan Bay.
Formed in 2010 by merging Changwon, Masan and Jinhae.
Changwon was one of Korea's first planned cities (1970s), built around a large machinery industrial complex.
Jinhae is famous for its cherry blossom festival.
Q3832: Capital of the Central African Republic, on the Ubangi River opposite DR Congo.
Founded as a French outpost in 1889 at the rapids that end river navigation from Brazzaville.
Badly affected by civil conflict since 2013.
Q243846: City in central Iraq on the Euphrates, next to the ruins of Babylon.
Capital of Babylon Governorate; founded around 1101.
Was a centre of Shia learning in the Middle Ages.
Nearby are ancient Borsippa and Kish.
Q3181093: Island upazila off the coast of Cox's Bazar District, Bangladesh.
Known for its lighthouse and salt production.
Very vulnerable to cyclones and erosion from the Bay of Bengal.
Q1758751: New town in the northwestern New Territories of Hong Kong, also called Castle Peak.
One of the earliest settlements in the Hong Kong area, used as a port in the Tang dynasty.
Developed as a new town from the 1970s; served by Light Rail.
Q58675: City in Hebei about 225 km northeast of Beijing; formerly Jehol (Rehe).
The Mountain Resort was the summer palace of the Qing emperors, larger than the Summer Palace in Beijing.
The Eight Outer Temples include a copy of Lhasa's Potala Palace (World Heritage Site).
Its local accent is said to be the closest to Standard Mandarin.
Q44255: Capital of Tucumán Province in northern Argentina, the country's smallest province.
Argentina declared its independence here on 9 July 1816; the Casa Histórica is a national monument.
Called the 'Garden of the Republic' for its sugar-cane fields.
Founded in 1565 and moved to its present site in 1685.
Q1218: Holy city for Judaism, Christianity and Islam, in the Judaean Mountains.
Its walled Old City contains the Western Wall, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Dome of the Rock (World Heritage Site).
Israel's seat of government; its status is disputed with the Palestinians, who claim East Jerusalem as their capital.
Over 3,000 years old; King David made it his capital.
Q1477270: The municipality of Mexicali, the northernmost municipality of Latin America.
Includes the city of Mexicali and the Mexicali Valley farmland, irrigated by the Colorado River.
Also contains islands in the Gulf of California.
Q81398: Port and resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast in Guerrero.
From 1565 the Manila galleons sailed between Acapulco and the Philippines for 250 years.
A glamorous resort of Hollywood stars in the 1950s–60s; famous for the La Quebrada cliff divers.
Badly damaged by Hurricane Otis in 2023.
Q198184: County-level city in Shandong under Weifang.
Known as 'Dinosaur City' for one of the world's largest dinosaur fossil sites.
Called Mizhou in the Song dynasty, when the poet Su Shi was its governor and wrote some of his best-known poems here.
